subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-supported through `deleteAfterRun`, or should recurring `deleteAfterRun` be rejected as a one-shot-only lifecycle flag?
rationale: This PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96045 intentionally choose opposite contracts for recurring `deleteAfterRun`, and automation should not rewrite the branch until maintainers pick the product behavior.

options.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Complete this PR's direction by handling existing persisted omitted jobs and reconciling or closing the strict-validation direction.

options.title: Adopt one-shot-only validation
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue through the strict-validation path after its UI, Gateway, and upgrade blockers are fixed.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only behavior
options.body: Merge only the new-job default and document that existing omitted jobs still require operator action or a separate migration.

recommendation.title: Support recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Complete this PR's direction by handling existing persisted omitted jobs and reconciling or closing the strict-validation direction.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent focused cron normalization and store commits make this the best available routing owner for the default and persisted-upgrade contract choice.
